scope: Three reproduced maintenance defects; no new feature milestone.

corrections.observedDefect: A provider TextReserveError with an accessor or unreadable code could throw during legacy collection classification and suppress a healthy sibling app.
corrections.change: Capture a string code only from a safe own data descriptor. Unreadable metadata becomes app-local STORE_UNAVAILABLE; no provider accessors or messages are exposed. Global cancellation assertions retain precedence.
corrections.redPhase: Targeted accessor regression failed with the provider exception before the source fix.
regressionCoverage: Own and inherited code getters are not invoked
Healthy sibling read completes before return
Cancellation rejects the full batch without late plaintext

corrections.observedDefect: Pagehide before native collection bootstrap completed could leave a restored page displaying its loading placeholder with no actionable closed-state guidance.
corrections.change: Abort bootstrap and display closed-view guidance if the collection has not mounted. A mounted view retains ownership of its DOM and plaintext cleanup; late fetch/body completions cannot remount.
regressionCoverage: Pagehide before response or body completion

corrections.observedDefect: Displaying authenticated recovered text through a textarea or EasyMDE could normalize line endings, changing unedited exports and falsely marking the snapshot as edited.
corrections.change: Retain the recovered source and its rendered baseline. Export exact recovered text while the displayed value is unchanged; genuine edits export the current editor value. Cleanup clears both baselines.
regressionCoverage: TXT and JSON retain BOM, CRLF and bare CR before editing on /text/, /apps/textarea/ and /apps/markdown/
Editor normalization alone does not label a user edit
Real editor changes export the edited value
Pagehide clears drafts and revokes download URLs

validation.counting: 110 distinct source/DOM cases plus 3 installed-package/integration cases. The 16 legacy and 17 combined collection cases repeated against the installed SDK are not added to the distinct total.

assertions: Separate native v1 and v2 builds
No synthetic or issuer endpoints in native assets
Installed public SDK and strict TypeScript
Fresh B-only recovery with A listener closed
Store loss, same-state restart, missing/corrupt app isolation
No recovery writes or state/quota changes

installedLegacyCollectionReplay.method: Copy the unchanged tests/text-collection.mjs body into a temporary fresh installed consumer, replacing only its relative SDK import with @continuitykit/account-reserve/text-reserve; run Node test and remove the fixture.

environmentNotes: Initial package attempts stopped before assertions because the sandbox could not write the standard npm cache; an older temporary cache then lacked a required cached package.
A fresh writable temporary cache was populated only from existing cached public registry packages named by the pinned lockfile. All installs remained offline; no dependency or lockfile changed.
The first actual-store attempts stopped at sandbox loopback-listen restrictions. The same two unchanged tests passed after narrowly approved permission for disposable local synthetic servers.
An initial ad-hoc stdin replay invocation encountered the generator CLI argv guard before tests ran; correcting only the temporary runner invocation allowed the installed legacy suite to pass.

review.scope: Internal maintenance review and local regression validation, not an external security audit.
review.selfServiceIndependentReview: Root reported independent internal review with no remaining finding.

hosted.rejection: The proposed publication would send a live source-repository credential to an existing terminal outside the managed sandbox/network proxy. Automatic review rejected the avoidable credential exposure and unauthorized repository access risk.

limitations: Installed recovery uses synthetic credentials and disposable local stores, not physical passkeys or independent providers.
Native UI evidence executes source under JSDOM; successful native builds do not establish physical-browser behavior.
The self-service export test uses controlled recovery data and actual compiled editor modules; it is not a new hosted recovery test.
These maintenance corrections provide no evidence of demand, retained adoption or prize outcomes.
